intended_object: The canonical isomorphism from the universal coefficient theorem between local cohomology and the dual of local homology, Hⁿ(M, M∖{x}; R, N) ≅ Hom_k(Hₙ(M, M∖{x}; R), N), given by the relative Kronecker map at a point x that has a Euclidean chart (Hatcher §3.1, §3.3). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body uses the library's general relative universal-coefficient equivalence `TopPair.singularKroneckerEquivOfProjectiveHomology` for the pair (M, M∖{x}). That equivalence is the relative Kronecker map, packaged as a linear equivalence once it is shown to be bijective. Its hypothesis, that relative homology is projective in every degree, is supplied by `projective_singularHomology_complSingleton`. That lemma holds because local homology is R in degree dim E and zero in every other degree, and R is projective. The `_apply` lemma confirms that the map is the Kronecker map. So the definition is exactly the stated canonical isomorphism.

The hypotheses fit the intended setting. The chart at x (an open partial homeomorphism to a finite-dimensional real normed space) and the T₁ assumption are what make the local-homology computation work. Projectivity of R is needed: without it, the Ext¹(H_{n-1}, N) term of the universal coefficient sequence need not vanish, and the Kronecker map need not be an isomorphism.

The fully general version, for any pair whose homology is projective, already exists in the library as `TopPair.singularKroneckerEquivOfProjectiveHomology`. This declaration is just its specialization to local cohomology, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no singular cohomology or universal coefficient theorem, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
